subject: zenGarden
pitch: A small Japanese garden diorama on a square base. A curved red wooden bridge over a koi pond with three orange and white koi, a stone lantern, a little pine tree with cloud-shaped foliage, a cherry tree in full pink blossom dropping petals, raked white gravel with a few mossy rocks, and stepping stones leading to the bridge.
reasoning:
I'm planning out the diorama components—base, bridge, pond, koi, lantern, trees, gravel, stones—and thinking through how to build them with the SDK using basic primitives like boxes, cylinders, spheres, and cones, plus sweep operations for curved elements.

I'm structuring the build around a single root joint with props attached as plain parts, since the scenery doesn't need rigging. I'm sizing the base slab at roughly 2.4m square and deciding how to represent the pond as a shallow basin with a recessed water surface, while working out the overall layout coordinates for placing each element.

Planning the gravel texture and raked-sand pattern using a grain paint effect, and figuring out dimensions for the pond's dark teal water plane and surrounding stone rim so it sits believably within the dug-out area of the base.

I'm scaling a cylinder geometry to make an oval-shaped pond basin, then placing stone rocks manually around its rim with computed angular positions. For the arched wooden bridge, I'm deciding to span it along the Z-axis across the pond so it reads clearly from the viewer's front-facing perspective, adjusting the pond's center position to accommodate the crossing.

Now I'm defining the bridge deck using a swept box section following a Catmull curve that arcs upward in the middle and touches down on both banks, plus adding simple railing rails as parallel offset sweeps on either side of the deck.

Adding railing sweeps and support posts...

Now I'm designing the koi for the pond—three orange-and-white fish with painted spots swimming along curved paths beneath the water surface, and figuring out the layered depths for pond water, gravel, and basin.

I'll settle on koi sitting visibly on the water surface, then build each koi as a swept body along a curved path with a tapered radius profile to get that tapered fish shape from head to tail.

Writing fish radius function...

For color I'll bring in the spots paint helper for the orange-white koi pattern, pulling from the same builder package as the other paint utilities.

For the tail fin, since the fish lies flat on the water's surface, I'm orienting the extrude so its thickness runs vertically — forward direction as outline x, sideways as outline y, giving a flat horizontal fin. I'll build the fish as a function taking center position, heading, and seed, placing the tail at the rear and head at the front along the local z-axis before rotating into world space.

Defining the tail fin outline as a fan shape spreading backward from the attachment point, with a thin extrusion thickness, then moving on to think about color patterns on the koi body using a paint function for spots.

I'm figuring out the koi coloring using a spots function with warm cream and orange tones, plus tiny dark spheres for eyes near the head. For placement, I'm working out how high to float the koi in the water so they appear half-submerged, and I'm laying out the pond's gravel slab and water disc heights relative to the base.

I'm positioning the pond as an elliptical disc with the bridge crossing over it at x=0, making sure the deck spans the pond width while checking that koi fish placed at various angles and positions don't collide with the bridge's footprint.

Now I'm checking that koi positioned near the pond edges stay clear of the arching deck's underside, confirming the deck's curved height keeps it above the water-level koi throughout. For the pine tree, I'm planning a cloud-shaped canopy made of flattened, scaled sphere clusters in dark green stacked at different heights above a tapered brown trunk.

For the cherry tree, I'm sketching a dark trunk with curved sweep-based branches and considering blossom clusters made from small pink spheres or card textures using SVG-rendered petal shapes for a more delicate look.

Still working out petal cards...

Now I'm placing the cherry tree itself: a trunk with curved taper, branches radiating from the top, and a canopy built from scattered blossom cards distributed within an ellipsoid volume around the crown. I'm figuring out the card count and density needed for a convincing canopy without overloading the mesh.

For the stone lantern, I'm structuring it in tiers: a base, pillar, lantern box with a dark opening, and a roof. I'm approximating the flared pyramid roof using a four-sided cone geometry rotated 45 degrees to give it that stylized stone-lantern look.

Now I'm working out the exact stacked heights for each component — foot, pillar base, pillar shaft, capital, and lantern chamber — computing their y-positions sequentially so they sit properly on top of the gravel.

Then I'm adding windows to each face of the lantern chamber, a pyramidal roof sitting centered above the chamber, and a small finial cone with a sphere cap on top, totaling roughly 1.0m tall, before deciding where to place the whole lantern relative to the scene's front-left area.

Now I'm placing the lantern near the bridge end and working out stone colors for the lantern and a warm glowing window hue. For the mossy rocks, I'm planning to use flattened spheres sunk slightly into the ground with a mottled paint technique blending stone grey and moss green, while narrowing down which helper functions I actually need to import from the builder module.

For the stepping stones leading up to the bridge, I'm sketching out a path of flattened stone shapes positioned between the front edge of the base and the bridge's near end, adjusting their z-coordinates so they connect smoothly from the ground into the bridge deck.

For the base itself, I'm designing a square diorama frame in dark wood tone with a gravel slab inset on top, adding raked grain texture lines across it to suggest a rock garden pattern.

I'm considering adding a concentric ring pattern to the gravel paint, computing radial distance from center and alternating two shades to simulate raked rings around the pond, then defining the water color separately as a deep teal.

I'm also planning rim stones scattered around the pond's elliptical edge using scaled angle positions, then working out the bridge deck height curve across the span and sketching railing posts and swept rails along the bridge sides using curve interpolation.

Now I'm thinking through the deck's cross-section sweep along its path, confirming orientation so the box section sits flat with sideways extent matching the bridge width, and settling on a red lacquered wood color for the railings. I'm noting I'll need the rng helper for randomized stone placement, the frame helper for oriented cards, and texture imports for surface details.

Setting up the garden scene...

Adding the pond water surface as a thin cylinder sitting just above the gravel, slightly raised so it reads as a pool, then placing the koi a bit above that.

Scattering rim stones around the pond's edge using randomized radius and angle, partially sinking them into the ground for a natural look.

Writing koi fish function...

Still tuning the body radius formula...

Working through fish body proportions...

I'll make the radius function return a wider sideways radius with a shorter vertical one to flatten the koi body, then apply painted spot coloring with randomized seeds per fish before sweeping the body along a smoothed path. Now I'm sketching the tail fin extrusion using an outline and orientation vectors.

Working out fin apex placement...

Each koi gets two tiny dark eye spheres, and I'm skipping pectoral fins for simplicity. Setting the koi's vertical position relative to the water surface, then placing three koi at different spots within the pond's elliptical bounds, checking each fish's heading vector so its body stays inside the pond edges.

I'm checking that the bridge deck and posts sit well above the koi's swimming depth, so there's no visual collision between them, then placing flattened cylinder stepping stones with a lighter stone color and slight scale distortion for irregularity. Now I'm starting the pine tree's trunk using a curved sweep through a few control points with a tapering radius from base to top.

I'm adding outward-reaching branches as tapered rods, then layering sphere-based cloud puffs for the pine's canopy at varying heights, offsets, and vertical squash, with a few puffs tinted a paler green for light patches. I'm checking that the lowest puff sits just above the bare trunk so the foliage reads as floating cloud shapes over visible bark, and now moving on to set up the cherry tree's position.

For the cherry, I'm sweeping a curved trunk path with tapering radius, then adding several branches as thin tapered sweeps radiating outward from points along the trunk toward different tip directions. For the canopy, I'm generating a scatter of randomly placed blossom card frames within an ellipsoid region using rejection sampling.

I'm designing a five-petal blossom flower as an SVG texture, with pink ellipse petals rotated around a center and a small yellow circle core, sized to fit within the viewBox cleanly.

Now I'm scattering fallen petals flat on the gravel ground near the tree base using card frames with varied flow directions, plus adding a separate batch of petals mid-air around the tree at different heights and tilts to simulate them drifting down from the canopy.

Next I'm building a lantern helper function, then mossy rock meshes using a mottled stone-and-moss texture with a flattened dome shape and a small green moss cap on top, and finally placing a cluster of these rocks at a few positions near the bridge and tree.

For the base, I'm considering adding a thin darker trim border around the wood platform for visual polish but deciding it's optional and can be skipped for conciseness. For the lantern, I'm adding glowing window panels on each of the four faces of the chamber and a four-sided pyramid roof rotated to align its edges properly.

I'm now stacking up the lantern's tiers carefully: foot, pillar base, shaft, capital, chamber, and roof cone, checking each segment's height and center position so they connect seamlessly from bottom to top, with stone and roof colors assigned and the roof overhanging slightly beyond the chamber walls.

Next I'm checking whether the lantern's placement near the pond overlaps anything—verifying it sits outside the pond rim and clear of the bridge deck—then reviewing the stepping stone coordinates to make sure their radius doesn't collide with the bridge's end point.

That gap near the ground is small enough to ignore, and the front edge stones line up fine. Now I'm defining the deck curve as a parabolic height function across z positions and generating the deck points to sweep the geometry through.

For the railings, I'm placing points slightly above the deck curve at each z-slice, sweeping thin red cylinders along them, and adding vertical posts at intervals so they sit flush on the deck edges at x = ±0.19. The spacing and heights all line up correctly with the deck curve.

Now I'm moving to the koi and cherry tree details, using a seeded random generator for the rim stones and blossoms. For the canopy I'm rejection-sampling points inside an ellipsoid to scatter around 150 blossom positions, then assigning each a loose random orientation frame so the clusters feel organic rather than uniform. I'm layering in a few pale pink puff spheres of varying size and offset around the canopy center to build up the cherry blossom volume before adding the blossom cards themselves.

Then I'm scattering fallen petals on the ground as flat cards lying face-up with a radial flow pattern, plus a separate batch of petals suspended in the air falling at angled trajectories with downward drift vectors. For the raked gravel I'm computing distance from the pond center and using a sine wave on that distance to alternate between two gravel tones, creating concentric ring patterns. The pond water gets a mottled blend between two teal/blue colors, and I'm starting on the koi fish spot pattern mixing white and orange paint.

Now I'm defining a helper function that builds a koi fish by establishing forward and side vectors based on heading angle, then generating an S-shaped body curve using sine-based lateral offsets at several points along the fish length, and a radius function that tapers the body width using a power curve for a more natural fish silhouette.

Still writing fish geometry...

I'm adding a smaller flattened moss cap on top of each rock sphere, double-checking that the rock's buried bottom stays hidden inside the base box and that the moss layer sits just above the rock's highest point.

Now I'm sketching out the pine and cherry tree placement functions, then defining the color palette (bark brown, pine greens, red, stone grays, orange and white for koi, water tones) along with blossom pink. I'm setting up the import of builder utilities (catmull, createBuilder, frame, mottle, paint, rng, spots, svg) and starting the main build function with the garden metadata and root joint at the origin.

Writing the base platform, gravel layer, and pond geometry...

Now I'm placing the pond rim stones along an elliptical path with slight random offsets, then positioning the koi fish with specific headings and checking they don't collide with the bridge deck or each other. Verifying the deck clearance above the koi and confirming the ellipse bounds keep everything within the pond, then moving on to the lantern, pine, cherry tree, and remaining rocks before finalizing the blossom card texture and extrude calls.

Writing sweep and rod geometry for the pine branches, cherry trunk, and cherry canopy branches using catmull-rom curves with tapered radii and bark coloring, defining tip coordinates for the cherry blossoms...
